title: Flow Cytometry Protocol for Cell Staining and Analysis
author: Yuan Yao
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.p9ndr5e
materials: Adjust the threshold of Hoechst with 5000;

steps.title: Grow cells to target density
steps.instruction: Cultivate cells in ABTGcasa medium at 37 °C until OD₄₅₀ reaches 0.15.

steps.title: Add antibiotics for several generations
steps.instruction: Supplement the culture with rifampicin at 300 µg ml⁻¹ and cephalexin at 10 µg ml⁻¹ and continue growth for three to four generations.

steps.title: Harvest cells by cold centrifugation
steps.instruction: Collect the cells by centrifugation performed at 4 °C.

steps.title: Fix cells in ethanol
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet in 70 % ethanol.

steps.title: Wash cells with Tris buffer
steps.instruction: Wash the ethanol‑fixed cells by centrifugation and resuspend in Tris‑HCl buffer pH 7.5.

steps.title: Stain DNA with Hoechst
steps.instruction: Add Hoechst 33258 to the cell suspension and incubate on ice for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare sample for cytometer
steps.instruction: After staining and washing, resuspend the cell pellet in 0.5 mL of appropriate buffer for cytometer sample uptake.

steps.title: Set cytometer flow rate
steps.instruction: Adjust the cytometer to a low flow speed delivering approximately 100–1000 cells per second (avoid rates below 100 or above 1000 cells s⁻¹).

steps.title: Acquire data
steps.instruction: Once the flow rate is stable, record data for 10,000 cells.
